handbookNote: Utah Commercial Driver's License Handbook (2025 Edition, base AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System'/2005 CDL Testing System content -- cover page stamped 'Version: March 2025', with individual section-footer revision stamps ranging from July 2017 to March 2025 depending on section), published by the Utah Driver License Division (DLD, dld.utah.gov), a division of the Utah Department of Public Safety -- the SAME agency that publishes Utah's non-commercial Driver Handbook already built in this project, and confirmed (per this project's prior Utah Driver-track research) to be distinct from Utah's Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV, dmv.utah.gov), which handles vehicle/vessel registration and titling, not driver/CDL testing. Fetched directly from https://dld.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026-COMPLIANT_CDL-Manual.pdf on 2026-08-23 (6.9MB PDF), full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/ut_cdl_research/ut_cdl_manual_full.txt (9,833 lines). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED, partially HEDGED. CONFIRMED directly from two official dld.utah.gov pages independent of the manual (the manual itself never states knowledge-test item counts or a passing-score percentage anywhere in the fetched text, confirmed by exhaustive keyword search for 'questions', 'percent', '80%', and similar terms -- same situation as this project's Montana/Louisiana/New Mexico CDL builds): (1) from https://dld.utah.gov/cdl-info/, verified by two independent exhaustive numeric-listing fetches -- the Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement written knowledge test is 30 questions and the Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement written knowledge test is 20 questions (the X endorsement has no separately-published combined count; the manual itself states X requires passing both the H and N component tests). (2) from https://dld.utah.gov/cdl-driving-test/, verified with a direct-quote exhaustive numeric-listing fetch -- the Basic Control Skills Test (4 exercises: Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, Reverse Offset Backing) is passed with 'eight or fewer error points,' and the on-road Driving Skills Test is passed with '30 or fewer error points'; the CDL Skills Test has three segments (vehicle inspection, basic control, on-road) taken in that order, each must be passed before the next; a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP/CDIP) must be held at least 14 days before the skills test and is valid 180 days; the skills-test fee is $78 for two attempts / $52 per retake; applicants must be 18+ with at least 1 year of prior Class D license experience; a Medical Examiner's Certificate is valid up to 24 months. An initial WebFetch pass surfaced additional endorsement item counts (doubles/triples, passenger, school bus, and an X-endorsement total) that could NOT be reproduced on a second independent exhaustive-numeric-listing fetch of the same page and are NOT actually present in the page's text -- these were discarded as likely small-model fetch-summarization artifacts rather than treated as confirmed facts, per this project's verification discipline. HEDGED (never disclosed in the manual text or on the DLD website, confirmed absent by exhaustive search of both): the General Knowledge test's item count and passing-score percentage, and the item counts for the Air Brakes, Combination Vehicles, Doubles/Triples, Passenger, and School Bus knowledge tests. The federally standardized 80% minimum passing score under 49 CFR 383.135(a) applies regardless of any state disclosure. Third-party CDL test-prep aggregators (not used as a source for any question content, cited here only as corroboration) converge on a conventional 50-question/80%-passing General Knowledge format consistent with the AAMVA base manual used by other CDL-track states in this project, but this specific item count and passing percentage are NOT asserted as officially confirmed Utah figures anywhere in this question bank -- no numeric value in this bank was carried over from another state's manual. Content-depth rationale: Utah uses the same AAMVA-authored base manual structure as several other CDL-track states in this project, organized into the same 13 core sections plus Utah-specific front matter woven into Section 1 -- Section 1 Introduction (CDL classes/endorsements/restriction codes, Utah-specific requirements, medical self-certification, disqualifications), Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering 2.1 Vehicle Inspection through roughly 2.16 Mountain Driving, 03_driving_safely_b covering 2.17 Driving Emergencies through the end of the section, including ABS, skids, fires, and the alcohol/BAC-effects table), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Material (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering 9.1 Intent of the Regulations through 9.4 Loading and Unloading, 11_hazmat_b covering 9.5 Bulk Packaging Marking through 9.7 Hazardous Materials Emergencies, explicitly excluding the 9.8 Glossary since the manual states in a parenthetical note that test-takers 'will not be tested on this glossary'), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection, and Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test combined with Section 13 On-Road Driving into one bucket (this project's established convention for the manual's two shortest sections). Sections 3 (Cargo, 22 questions), 8 (Tank Vehicles, 18 questions), and 7 (Doubles/Triples, 24 questions) are naturally short in this manual and their buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections; Section 6 (Combination Vehicles, 68 questions) and Section 9 (Hazardous Material, split across two buckets totaling 103 questions) supported deeper coverage and were sized up accordingly, reflecting the manual's real step-by-step procedural depth in those sections (e.g. Section 6's coupling procedure alone runs 16 steps, uncoupling 10, plus separate pintle-hook/drawbar/gooseneck variants). Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Utah manual text cited in that question's source_note, or in one of the two confirmed dld.utah.gov pages cited above where explicitly noted; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers. The full bank (665 questions before the build script's automatic dedup pass) was independently re-verified by the top-level agent directly against the source files (not taken on sub-agent self-report): every bucket file was parsed and checked for structural completeness, distinct 4-choice sets, and correct_choice letter balance (final bank-wide distribution A=25.7% / B=25.3% / C=25.1% / D=23.9%, all within the required 15-35% band per letter), and one genuine correct_choice/explanation mismatch found during spot-check review (a hazmat endorsement question-count item in the licensing bucket) was corrected before the build.
